input.content:
# How three US states run heat pump rebates in 2026
_Prepared 2026-10-25 · 3 sources_

## Bottom line
All three states pay more to lower-income households; amounts and stacking rules differ.

## Key findings
- California: income-tiered rebates up to $8,000 [1].
- New York: up to $10,000 for whole-home systems via contractors [2].
- Massachusetts: up to $10,000 per home, with an income-eligible enhanced tier [3].

## Sources
1. Heat pump rebates 2026 — California Energy Office. https://energy.ca.example/heat-pump-rebates-2026
2. Heat pump programs — NYSERDA. https://nyserda.ny.example/programs/heat-pumps
3. Heat pump rebates — Mass Save. https://masssave.ma.example/rebates/heat-pumps

input.summary: All three states pay more to lower-income homes. California offers up to $8,000 (at or below 80% of area median income) and $3,000 otherwise. New York pays up to $10,000 for whole-home systems through contractors. Massachusetts pays up to $10,000, or up to $16,000 for income-eligible homes. All three pages were updated in 2026.

findings.detail: Whole-home incentives are paid to participating contractors and passed through to the customer, so the owner applies through an installer. Page updated 2026-05-12.
